chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Nasr from Dawud ibn Sirran said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had a debt of dinars against another man, so he transferred it to him via a third party with dinars; should he take dirhams for them? He said, 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to settle a debt in a different currency than the one originally contracted?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the transfer of debt (hawalah) permits settling a gold-denominated obligation with silver, reflecting the practical flexibility of currency exchange in early Islamic jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the principle that the essence of hawalah lies in the discharge of the debt value rather than strict adherence to the original medium of exchange, a view supported by Shia scholars to facilitate commercial ease.
